I originally wasn't planning on filming something, but then I had a really shitty day today and thought I should talk about something that makes me happy. It's three in the morning. And I'm up in Europe to watch Vox Machina kill something. That's how much Critical Role means to me. Critical Role means to me is that even when we have sleepless nights, I still have something to watch and keep me company. I actually get up every Friday at 3:50am-- because I live in Germany-- before work to watch the show live. It's been a huge inspiration to me for storytelling purposes. It is one of the most imaginative forms of storytelling I've ever seen. What I see on screen is the exact same game I play with my friends, except I get to experience this one game with tens of thousands of other people. I obviously really like the characters. I find them very relatable and really inspirational. It means joy and excitement, but it also means crying for these characters that I've come to love so much. I really love being able to turn on-- I was about to say the telly. The Twitch, and see three badass women doing badass stuff every week. What Critical Role means to me is a sense of friendship. When I found Critical Role, I was instantly attracted to the friendship that existed between the cast members. As a retired soldier, it's easy to forget that there's still great people like you guys out there, so seriously, from the bottom of my heart, thank you. The story of Vox Machina means that there will always be friends that you can find and families that you can forge, who will keep on fighting their hardest with you, even when it feels like you've already lost the war. Okay, so Critical Role and what does it mean to me? It's been a tough year, dudes, and-- it's been a tough year. Critical Role got me through a lot of the rough days. I discovered Critical Role at a difficult time in my life. My brother had just passed away and life was crappy. It helped me to get through that really sucky time. Last year I had serious depression, anxiety, and so on. Essentially, I was having trouble getting to grips with what I was and who I wanted to be. It gave me something to cling to in a really dark time and made me beg my friends to play D&D and then send them sad D&D photos when we didn't. A little less than a year ago, I was in a very different place. I was depressed, and I didn't really see a point in living. And Critical Role changed that. Because it has gotten me through a particularly hard year, which started with my mom getting very sick and then passing away within six weeks of her cancer diagnosis. Critical Role has gotten me through the death of my grandfather, it has gotten me through the threat of homelessness, and it continues to get me through the constant stress of a close family member and their battle with cancer. To say you guys saved my life, I'm being literal. Before Critical Role, I was in a pretty bad place. My depression was at its all-time high, I had lost my core group of friends, and it had gotten so bad that I decided to end it. I knew everything that I was going to do. I even had a date set and planned. And that date came and went. For all intents and purposes, I was watching something so compelling that I forgot my plan. It didn't occur to me anymore. [music] I've said it before, but Critical Role was a light in the darkness for me. Critical Role really gave me hope. It's helped me get over the feeling that I can't keep doing the things I like to do, because of my age. And that everything's okay, that I can keep doing it. You're only as old as you think you are. I stumbled into this community and found a family. Because of Critical Role, I started DMing my very first campaign about a year ago, and it's been amazing since then. I've met a bunch of wonderful, fantastic people. The whole community around Critical Role got me into stuff that I never would have liked in the first place. The playlists got me into Chvrches and First Aid Kit. Patrick Rothfuss's guest appearance got me into the Kingkiller Chronicles, which I love. I've joined some amazing D&D games. I have started drawing and creating again, after pretty much giving up on it. I have grown so much as an artist and a person due to the support of all of you Critters out there. About a year ago, the cast decided that they liked some of my work, and asked me to do some t-shirts for them. Now, until that point, I was just a hobbyist, not really a graphic designer. But I'm going to be. And that's thanks to Critical Role. I have seen that there's so much more for me to explore as a performer, and it has rekindled my passion that had recently been waning. For this, I could not be more grateful. There once was a girl from New Jersey who loved many things that were nerdy. She cosplayed and crafted, but dice weren't added, 'til seeing that show late on Thursday. From watcher to player to DM, the obsession became quite extreme. Her dice bags did swell, and her shop's doing well, and it's all thanks to this nerdy stream. The fanart inspired me to try to start making art. I stink at it. Not good at it at all. Nope, not good at all. But I'm trying. When I first started watching these nerdy ass voice actors, I was a college dropout with no job. Now I'm a teacher whose OTP has officially gone canon. Twice! I'm not saying causation, but I'm definitely saying correlation. I work for a social service industry, and we primarily serve people with mental health issues and that are suffering from poverty. I've been granted the ability to start a Dungeons & Dragons group through my job, which I absolutely love, and I know my clients do, too. You guys are amazing, and thank you so much for sharing your beautiful, wonderful world with us. It means a lot. Thank you so much. Thank you. I just wanted to say thank you for giving me something to look forward to every week, and also I may or may not have a Slayer's Take tattoo. Is it Thursday yet?

name: MATT
dialogue: "Then I would not recommend taking folks to Fort Daxio, especially if it's sustained damage. "Well, we've been busy in Emon." The eyes glance over at Raishan. "And, well, needless to say, "things have gone a bit strange. We've been working with Spireling Shenn and the Clasp, and we've been "able to smuggle thousands of denizens of Emon beneath the city. Those that were not directly "enslaved or gave fealty to the Cinder King out of fear and other interests we've been able to keep "safe, and we've moved through the tunnels as often as possible. There are still many, many, many "wyvern riders that patrol the city; the townfolk have run out of offerings and are now being sent "out in slave groups to pull goods from nearby cities to bring at the feet of the dragon. We also "have a rising volcanic mass rising up beneath the city that has consumed a number of the underground "Clasp tunnels and has been slowly pinching off our mobility beneath the town, so our intent to "hopefully find some sort of retort or vengeance and eventually take down the dragon... that clock "is definitely ticking. Now. We've been keeping as best an eye on Thordak as we can. Brom, bless him "and his sacrifices, has been our front man for this. And we know the creature has been shedding "scales in places where jets of ever-burning flame now spark and burn the city itself. Wherever each "one of these scales falls, it seems to be a beacon or source of its own white-hot fire. So the city "is now a pitfall of its own right. The creature itself, the dragon, it has these jets that now "burst from underneath its armor, fire that licks beyond it. It has a crest of red crystals now that "begin to twist behind its horns and head, its eyes are like white-hot stars from the sky, it's... "It's still dragon-like, but something more primal and elemental. (sighs) I'm not entirely certain "what we're dealing with here. But Brom, you've made some headway." And Brom clears his throat. "(ahem) Myself and a few devout have been doing our best to prepare surviving warriors and guards, "and mages who were ousted from the Lyceum; we have a few strike teams that have been effective in "harrying the outside of his defenses, learning information we can, knocking down the guardians. "Since the fire giants have arrived it's been a little more difficult, so we've been reduced to "stealth missions, quick in and out. We don't have the muscle to assault head-on. Up until recently." His eyes pass over to you. "You say there are armies making their way to the city, and we have "you, all the strength that you've gained and the stories I've heard from people here at Whitestone. "If we're going to do something, we need to do it soon. Now, the Lyceum has fallen to those that "have sworn fealty to the Cinder King, so we don't have use of those artifacts anymore. We've been "trying to break through to the inner sanctum of the Cloudtop, what the dragon now calls its home, "its lair. It's burrowed this deep, underground basin where it resides now. It only emerges when "summoned or called to, or when it decides to make a proclamation, drawing what little bit of "children or families that it sees as a fun bit of play to watch them bow and quiver in the street "before asking for someone to prove their strength and their worship of himself and strike them where "they stand. Some days he's angry, some days he's laughing; this dragon is completely insane, we "can't really gauge. Red dragons are known for pride, and you could count on that, use it against "them, but sometimes his jaws quiver as he cries and shakes and yells out laughing into the sky, a "terrible laughter, one that can induce the worst of nightmares. I don't know what we're dealing "with anymore. However. We did have one team, a very brave team, that provoked the dragon to leave "its lair, and held it long enough for us to move past it and pierce the inside of its sanctum. Now, "we passed the wards, and the pools of fire. The beast returned before we could get too far, and I "lost most of my men, myself barely surviving with my life, and the scars to tell of it. But the "beast is building something in that lair. Something it is guarding fiercely. And something "that it will not leave. Something that I think it has come to hold more dear than the city it now "presides over. If there is a key to piercing its pride, or if there is a reason to take it down, I "begin to fear what it's holding below the city. Now, by the might of the Wounded Mistress of "Knowledge, Ioun, in the channels in which we speak, that is all the information I have. I hope "it's helped in some way." And he sits down in his chair and clutches his holy symbol.

If we have a way in, to break the Cloudtop, we can battle it there, draw it from its "lair. Force it to possibly rescind within, and have our final battle there. dialogue: We should probably get close to Greyskull and see if we can enter through the tunnels.

name: LIAM
dialogue: I think that's our way, yeah.

name: SAM
dialogue: Yes, but we do have to rally with your pops, and also didn't we cut loose 55 soldiers to wander free in the desert from Daxio?

name: LAURA
dialogue: They're meeting the other armies.

name: SAM
dialogue: They're just going to form up?

name: LAURA
dialogue: Trust in them. They're soldiers, they'll be able to find their way.

name: SAM
dialogue: Right. But can we scry and figure out where this other army is? Maybe we'll go there? Or maybe we should scry on our old keep and go there. Those seem like two good locations.

name: TALIESIN
dialogue: I think scrying on the old keep and then letting everyone know-- we don't necessarily want everyone arriving at the same place as well, as long as there's a coordinated movement towards the city.

name: LAURA
dialogue: They can all start attacking and we can come in from the bottom.

name: SAM
dialogue: Sure, but we've told the approaching army nothing about any plan whatsoever.

name: TALIESIN
dialogue: We can call them if we need to.

name: MARISHA
dialogue: So we probably want different regiments flanking the city in different areas?

name: TALIESIN
dialogue: And then maybe the 50 men coming into the sewers to fight.

name: LIAM
dialogue: I feel like we want to catch up with our father's army before they're anywhere near the walls of the city, because, well, that'd be stupid.

name: TALIESIN
dialogue: We can go meet them if that's the next move.

name: SAM
dialogue: And strategize when we get there? Once we see their forces, and what they have to offer?

name: MARISHA
dialogue: Percy, do you still have that map of Emon?

name: TALIESIN
dialogue: Yes, somewhere.

name: LAURA
dialogue: We should probably talk to Gilmore as well, and let him know that he has to fucking join us.

name: MARISHA
dialogue: That he drew the short straw. We drew the short straw for him.

name: TALIESIN
dialogue: We should also collect some other allies, if we're going to head in this direction.

name: LAURA
dialogue: Of course.

name: SAM
dialogue: All right. Do you want to go talk to Gilmore, Vaxy-poo?

name: TALIESIN
dialogue: We're going to need a painter, you know a painter, we should bring a painter with us.

name: SAM
dialogue: A painter? To paint our exploits?

name: TALIESIN
dialogue: Yes, to paint our exploits. You have that portrait--

name: MARISHA
dialogue: Once again, Percy, I feel like that's small picture--

name: TALIESIN
dialogue: Is it small potatoes? Is it really, though?

name: LIAM
dialogue: We could find a jeweller right now. If that's what you're into.

name: SAM
dialogue: I have a man at a casino that I really need to get revenge on.

name: TALIESIN
dialogue: You might as well get it all done now, because you're not going to be able to do it later.

name: MARISHA
dialogue: 24 hours left alive!

name: LIAM
dialogue: Kynan? Kynan!

name: SAM
dialogue: All right.

name: TALIESIN
dialogue: But no, stock up on what-- again, Whitestone doesn't necessarily have a lot for us to gather--

name: SAM
dialogue: But we should bring any potions. How we doing on potions? Did you ever divvy up our last several potions?

name: LAURA
dialogue: I did divvy up our last potions, I feel like it might be smart to get some more, but the only place to really buy any is Vasselheim.

name: SAM
dialogue: Is that true?

name: LAURA
dialogue: I mean it's the only city still standing that we have access to immediately. We don't have a lot of time. The thing is, I feel like people in Vasselheim said they would help us, but I don't know how they'd get to Emon to help us in time.

name: SAM
dialogue: I know, an airship! Oh shit, where's our airship?

name: LAURA
dialogue: It's on its way.

name: SAM
dialogue: To where?

name: LIAM
dialogue: Emon. To Emon.

name: SAM
dialogue: Did we say Emon, or did we say Daxio?

name: MATT
dialogue: It was on its way to Daxio--

name: MARISHA
dialogue: They're redirecting to Emon.

name: SAM
dialogue: Thank God. We're sending it to a dragon instead of a fort on fire.

name: TALIESIN
dialogue: It does have weaponry.

name: LAURA
dialogue: Yeah. It's made to take on things attacking it.

name: TALIESIN
dialogue: It's designed to help keep him on the ground.

name: MARISHA
dialogue: Uh-huh, yeah, it's a giant balloon in the air--

name: LAURA
dialogue: It's not a balloon, actually--

name: TALIESIN
dialogue: Well, no, it's a giant crystal. It's-- I know I keep saying--

name: MARISHA
dialogue: I always think of it as a high-tech Hindenberg.

name: TALIESIN
dialogue: I know. Please don't say that. That's not funny.

name: LIAM
dialogue: That's a metaphor for Vox Machina.

name: MATT
dialogue: There you go. If there ever was one, yeah.

name: SAM
dialogue: All right. Besides gathering our forces here, gathering our potions here, and telling Gilmore, where are we going? Let's put it to a vote, as we always do, democratically. Grog?

name: MATT
dialogue: "Yes?"

name: SAM
dialogue: Grog, where would you like to go? To the army waiting just outside of Emon, or to our old ratty keep with nothing in it?

name: TALIESIN
dialogue: "I'd like to go to the--" I don't know.

name: LAURA
dialogue: I don't know what he wants.

name: MATT
dialogue: Percy's getting a little strange off to the side.

name: LAURA
dialogue: Wait, Travis is watching, so he can just text in, yeah. Grog is thinking about it. Grog is thinking really hard.

name: MATT
dialogue: He considers it for a second and goes, "Whatever makes me kill things faster."

name: LAURA
dialogue: That's good.

name: MARISHA
dialogue: Wait, have we rested?

name: MATT
dialogue: You did rest before coming here. You spent the evening in Fort Daxio.

name: MARISHA
dialogue: And then we teleported. No, Allura brought us here.

name: SAM
dialogue: Okay, putting it to a vote. Three choices. Ready? To your dad, to our keep, or to Vasselheim. I don't know why, but it's been mentioned.

name: MARISHA
dialogue: Hang on, I can scry on our keep.

name: LAURA
dialogue: Can't Allura send a message to them and let them know what our plan is, and then we don't have to actually bamf there?

name: SAM
dialogue: We don't have a plan!

name: TALIESIN
dialogue: Wherever we go, we can let everyone know what the plan and where we're going is.

name: LAURA
dialogue: I feel like what we need to do-- okay, here's what I think our plan should be.

name: SAM
dialogue: Lead us, O Mighty Vex.

name: LAURA
dialogue: I feel like we should tell the armies gathering to prepare to attack. We enter in where the Clasp is; we come in from the bottom up.

name: SAM
dialogue: So they're going to create a diversion for us?

name: LAURA
dialogue: Exactly. They take on the armies while we head straight to Thordak.

name: LIAM
dialogue: Dad creates a shit-storm at the wall, and we take advantage of that chaos.

name: SAM
dialogue: We have to communicate this to them.

name: TALIESIN
dialogue: Easy to do. We just send a message.

name: LAURA
dialogue: We could send a message, or we could bamf there and then bamf another place. It seems a lot of time wasted.

name: TALIESIN
dialogue: Yeah, easier just to send a message.

name: MATT
dialogue: Allura has been in communication and has been the information hub between most of these individuals.

name: LIAM
dialogue: How long did we say before Syldor reaches Emon?

name: MATT
dialogue: By about dusk the following day.

name: LIAM
dialogue: Dusk the following day. And you said afternoon right now? So a little more than 24 hours.

name: TALIESIN
dialogue: We can at least get into there and start communicating with the Clasp.

name: MARISHA
dialogue: We're not really in good standing with them.

name: TALIESIN
dialogue: I'm sure they'll be happy to see us, regardless.

name: MARISHA
dialogue: You think? I guess. Sure. It's like seeing that person you hated in high school after something terrible just happened. Happy for the familiarity.

name: SAM
dialogue: But now they're a little bit overweight and they work in an Applebee's.

name: MARISHA
dialogue: Sure, and it's a little gratifying?

name: SAM
dialogue: Yeah.

name: LIAM
dialogue: They can hate us, and we can deal with that afterward, if there is even an afterward.

name: TALIESIN
dialogue: They're businessmen; I doubt they hold grudges.

name: LAURA
dialogue: I'm sure they hold grudges.

name: TALIESIN
dialogue: Not until after the dragon's been taken care of.

name: LAURA
dialogue: Then they'll make us pay?

name: TALIESIN
dialogue: Yes. It's not profitable to kill us before the dragon is dead.

name: LIAM
dialogue: Also, somewhere in all this fracas, we need you to take care of us with food.

name: TALIESIN
dialogue: When it's time.

name: LIAM
dialogue: Right, when is the time?

name: TALIESIN
dialogue: I think once we're there.

name: MARISHA
dialogue: It lasts for 24 hours.

name: LAURA
dialogue: Before we head in.

name: LIAM
dialogue: In the keep, for old time's sake?

name: LAURA
dialogue: I don't think that's very smart.

name: TALIESIN
dialogue: Or in the sewers, for old time's sake. (laughter)

name: LIAM
dialogue: I mean underneath.

name: TALIESIN
dialogue: Hopefully, in the keep.

name: SAM
dialogue: So we have a clear plan, then?

name: TALIESIN
dialogue: We have a plan for dinner.

name: LIAM
dialogue: There's no guarantees, Scanlan.

name: SAM
dialogue: Where are we going? That's all I care about right now.

name: LIAM
dialogue: We're going to hell. Where do you think we're going? It's going to be fucking awful. You're probably going to be dead in 48 hours.

name: SAM
dialogue: Yeah, but we'll be together, and I don't think that I'll die.

name: LIAM
dialogue: You're adorable.

name: TALIESIN
dialogue: You're going to be in front, if anything.

name: MARISHA
dialogue: This is the worst of two extremes.

name: TALIESIN
dialogue: You should scry on Greyskull.

name: MARISHA
dialogue: Is anyone still there?

name: SAM
dialogue: Last time I looked in, there was some movement, or it looked like people had recently been there.

name: MARISHA
dialogue: Wasn't it Drexel? Dranzel?

name: SAM
dialogue: Nope, they're off somewhere else.

name: LAURA
dialogue: You said by sunset tomorrow is when they'll be at Emon?

name: MATT
dialogue: That's when they'll be there and ready.

name: LAURA
dialogue: Okay.

name: MATT
dialogue: If you want more information, you might have to talk to somebody who has that information.

name: LAURA
dialogue: Right. What we need to do is plan a time that they start the attack.

name: SAM
dialogue: Sure. We've got to get there first and suss it out, too. We haven't done any recon. This army of your father's, we have no idea how big it is, if they have archers, if they have an elite SWAT team task force--

name: TALIESIN
dialogue: How do you feel that will affect our plan?

name: SAM
dialogue: If we know we have an elite SWAT team task force, we can take them down with us into the sewers!

name: TALIESIN
dialogue: I can almost promise you they do not have an elite SWAT team task force.

name: LAURA
dialogue: They might have some stealthy--

name: TALIESIN
dialogue: Some stealthy individuals.

name: MARISHA
dialogue: We have friends of our own.

name: SAM
dialogue: Also, if we do any recon, we might know that oh, there's a big thing we need to have taken out before we can even get in. What if our keep is being surrounded?

name: MARISHA
dialogue: Okay. Hang on. Let me scry on the keep. This will answer plenty of questions, and then we'll go from there.

name: LAURA
dialogue: Scry away, Keyleth.

name: MARISHA
dialogue: Did we leave Laina there? Did we leave anyone there, or is it completely vacated?

name: LIAM
dialogue: It was chaos when we left.

name: MATT
dialogue: Yeah, it was absolute chaos. You pushed your servants through. Your staff still currently exists somewhere in Whitestone.

name: MARISHA
dialogue: I can't scry on a building, correct?

name: MATT
dialogue: Correct.

name: LIAM
dialogue: We fought Vorugal and then high-tailed it out of there; inside and gone.

name: MARISHA
dialogue: I can't scry on a building.

name: TALIESIN
dialogue: Can you scry on a plant?

name: SAM
dialogue: Can you scry on a dead thing?

name: MARISHA
dialogue: Can I scry on a plant?

name: TALIESIN
dialogue: There is a tree.

name: MATT
dialogue: Because you are a druid, being a nature-based entity and it is a living creature... (laughter) Don't steal my thunder!

name: MARISHA
dialogue: One that I've had personal communications with.

name: MATT
dialogue: I would say, due to the fact that you are a druid and nature is your basis, if it is a specific plant-based entity that you are very familiar with, sure.

name: SAM
dialogue: Do we have anything like that at our keep?

name: MATT
dialogue: You have a number of trees in the front; you have the garden that you built in Sarenrae's temple.

name: MARISHA
dialogue: That's what I want to scry on. I want to start there.

name: MATT
dialogue: Okay.

name: MARISHA
dialogue: You know how it's always, "you zoom in really fast, and you zoom in really fast--" Can I slow down?

name: MATT
dialogue: It doesn't work that way.

name: MARISHA
dialogue: I can't pull focus?

name: MATT
dialogue: In theory, scrying is only supposed to show you what's there. I narratively let a little bit of a journey happen. You can't control the journey, sorry.

name: SAM
dialogue: DVR it.

name: MARISHA
dialogue: It's the worst. Okay.

name: MATT
dialogue: All right, so where are you doing the spell?

name: MARISHA
dialogue: Where?

name: MATT
dialogue: Where are you doing your Scry ritual?

name: MARISHA
dialogue: Not near the ziggurat, if we're still there.

name: MATT
dialogue: Right, so are you guys heading back to the castle, then?

name: LAURA
dialogue: Yeah, let's go to the castle.

name: MATT
dialogue: While you guys are heading back to the castle from underneath the tunnels, you are briefly headed off by a familiar dwarven fellow in robes and a crystalline staff: Elementalist Drake Thunderbrand. "By the way, before you leave, we've been working on a few things for you. They should "be of assistance to you. Come find me in the common room whenever you're ready."

name: SAM
dialogue: Yeah, sure. Wow, fortuitous.

name: MARISHA
dialogue: I like presents.

name: MATT
dialogue: You head to your quarters to do the Scry spell? Okay. Your vision clarifies on dark clouds. Your vision sees a gathering of grayish mists, and you slowly transition through them to see shapes that are either extremely small or extremely distant. Your vision begins to funnel through it quickly, like you're passing over the edge of a waterfall. There's a rush, and you see, as the clouds dissipate, a glimpse of the overhead of Emon. You see the once-gleaming city of white across the Bladeshimmer Shoreline pockmarked with black and tall towers of curling black smoke. You see flames that still burn unfettered, unstopped throughout the town, and what looks from the distance like small clouds of gnats or flies that you realize are much larger flying entities doing small passes over various neighborhoods to keep watch or find food. Your vision jumps again, this time careening down even faster. Below, you can see, from an overhead view, Greyskull Keep. You begin to rush in that direction, and as it gets closer, you can see the same damage it took from the wall from the initial attack of the Conclave. You see elements of rubble around the outside, though it's still pristine, being repaired by the celestial entity that was summoned by Pike shortly after. Your vision jumps again, this time through the repaired stained-glass exterior of the temple of Sarenrae, and it comes to rest there in a moment, amongst the strangely contrasting, peaceful greenery of this temple. There's such a sense of hopelessness and horror on the outside of the city, this one little moment of time here is almost like a time capsule of how things were before. It's sad, but hopeful at the same time. As your vision swivels over to the tree, there in the temple, while contained here for as long as it's been, it seems to be healthy. Looking in the vicinity, most everything seems in place.

name: MARISHA
dialogue: Do the trees look overgrown? Do the plants look overgrown?

name: MATT
dialogue: As much as being away for the handful of months that you have been. They look like they haven't been trimmed or tended to recently.

name: MARISHA
dialogue: And the temple is intact? It looks like the keep is still intact from where we rebuilt it?

name: MATT
dialogue: Correct. It has not fallen.

name: MARISHA
dialogue: Do I sense any movement?

name: MATT
dialogue: Make a perception check with disadvantage through your Scry spell.

name: TALIESIN
dialogue: No, I can't help. Yeah, no.

name: MARISHA
dialogue: I rolled two ones. Both ones. I'll say that's just flushing it out.

name: MATT
dialogue: Strangely, somehow through a Scry spell, something got in your eye in the temple.

name: MARISHA
dialogue: I hate it when the VR goggles short out. (laughter)

name: MATT
dialogue: You don't know if it's divine energy interference or what, but it stings a lot, and you feel the essence of the spell begin to shiver and quake, and as you try and clear your vision through, it remains blurred.

name: MARISHA
dialogue: Shit.

name: MATT
dialogue: You're still there; your presence is there, but you don't have the capability of seeing anything beyond the tree you're focused on. The Scry spell is focused on the tree, and everything around it has this hazy fog-of-war feel about five feet beyond it.

name: SAM
dialogue: Good scry.

name: MARISHA
dialogue: Good scry, guys. Good scry.

name: LAURA
dialogue: What did you see? Anything good? Are we safe?

name: MARISHA
dialogue: It's still standing, for the most part. I saw Pike's-- wait, her celestial being wasn't still there.

name: MATT
dialogue: No, it was temporarily summoned for the reconstruction of the ceiling portion.

name: MARISHA
dialogue: Looks okay. Looks like home.

name: LIAM
dialogue: Still standing? There wasn't anybody around it?

name: MARISHA
dialogue: I couldn't tell.

name: SAM
dialogue: How's my comic book collection? Is it still there?

name: MARISHA
dialogue: Burned.

name: TALIESIN
dialogue: Mint in box.

name: LIAM
dialogue: That's as close to a guarantee as we're going to get.

name: MARISHA
dialogue: I told you to get a fire box.

name: LAURA
dialogue: Do you think Drake would join us?

name: SAM
dialogue: Who? Little guy? I'd like to be the shortest on this trip, please.

name: LAURA
dialogue: Got it.

name: LIAM
dialogue: You are.

name: SAM
dialogue: Oh.

name: MARISHA
dialogue: Where's Kash?

name: LAURA
dialogue: And Zahra?

name: MARISHA
dialogue: Kash was really mad at us last time we talked to him.

name: LAURA
dialogue: So maybe we shouldn't ask him.

name: TALIESIN
dialogue: Let's not.

name: MARISHA
dialogue: I talked to him last time.

name: LAURA
dialogue: I don't even want Kash to come. I don't even want him around.

name: SAM
dialogue: When we walk near his residence, let's walk around.

name: LIAM
dialogue: That guy is a badass motherfucker, and we do want him.

name: SAM
dialogue: I know why you want him to come.

name: LIAM
dialogue: Well, he's got those brown eyes.

name: LAURA
dialogue: No, he's got one brown eye and one blue eye, I think.

name: TALIESIN
dialogue: We are this loopy because we're genuinely terrified, and we're doing everything we can not to go.

name: LIAM
dialogue: It's called gallows humor.

name: LAURA
dialogue: I'm going to go ask Zahra if she'll join us. Can I go talk to Zahra?

name: MATT
dialogue: Sure.

name: LIAM
dialogue: I'll go find Shaun, after her.

name: MARISHA
dialogue: You guys are forcing me into going and talking to Kash, aren't you?

name: LAURA
dialogue: Scanlan can ask him. It doesn't have to be you.

name: MARISHA
dialogue: Scanlan?

name: SAM
dialogue: Would you prefer me to go? We do have a rapport.

name: LAURA
dialogue: I do want to ask Jarett to come too, though.

name: SAM
dialogue: Oh, I need to go see Jarett. (laughter) You're on Kash duty, Kiki.

name: LIAM
dialogue: Scanlan, do you need a little resolve for this fight?

name: SAM
dialogue: I just want to see Jarett. He's our most solid ally, and most dependable friend.

name: LIAM
dialogue: There's no other reason?

name: SAM
dialogue: He's been there for us in our time of need.

name: LIAM
dialogue: Still no other reason?

name: SAM
dialogue: I feel like it would be a big pick-me-up to see him. (laughter)

name: LIAM
dialogue: Solid. You do that.

name: TALIESIN
dialogue: I'm going to talk to Cassandra about one last dip into the vaults to see if there's any potions. We know we have to leave them with something in case everything goes wrong, but anything we can take with us will be helpful, and then I have to fix this giant mess of parts that are currently in my bag. I may need to spend a little money. I do apologize.

name: LAURA
dialogue: Darling.

name: TALIESIN
dialogue: Okay, just letting you know. It might be a bit expensive to get everything working again.

name: LIAM
dialogue: Percy, spend it all.

name: TALIESIN
dialogue: I will not spend it all. I promise.

name: LAURA
dialogue: I gave an entire bag of jewels to a random efreet.

name: TALIESIN
dialogue: That was brazen, yes.

name: MARISHA
dialogue: We got armor out of it, though. It's not like we didn't get something from it.

name: TALIESIN
dialogue: If anyone asks about the plan, the plan is chaos, if everyone agrees with this. We want to break up their forces as much as possible. We want them sending ten percent of their forces to every edge of the city. They know where we're going; they know we're eventually heading to the center, and he's not going to leave anymore, but we're going to make it very difficult for them. They're either going to be fighting us in every corner, or they're going to be letting the entire city fall back to us.

name: LAURA
dialogue: I'm going to go find Zahra.

name: SAM
dialogue: Splitting the party five ways.

name: MARISHA
dialogue: I go find Kash.

name: MATT
dialogue: Okay. Vex, as you progress up to the secondary floor to the outside of Zahra's room, the door is closed.

name: LAURA
dialogue: Zahra, dear?

name: MATT
dialogue: Zahra, you hear a knock at your door.

name: MARY
dialogue: Hello? (laughter) What is it, darling? I'm trying to sleep.

name: LAURA
dialogue: Oh!

name: SAM
dialogue: This is where the live studio audience is supposed to applaud. (laughter)

name: MARISHA
dialogue: You had one job, pit crew.

name: TALIESIN
dialogue: You had five jobs--

name: MATT
dialogue: You had 12 jobs, pit crew.

name: MARY
dialogue: Anything in my eyes?

name: LAURA
dialogue: Not much time to sleep, I'm afraid.

name: MARY
dialogue: Unfortunately, I've been buried in books.

name: LAURA
dialogue: Yes, and plans are moving ahead much faster than we anticipated.

name: MARY
dialogue: First off, I heard word about a white dragon. Sister killer! (laughter) Yes, we have to go get tattoos. Tell me, what's the news? Catch me up.

name: LAURA
dialogue: We're marching on Emon tomorrow.

name: MARY
dialogue: Oh! I was going to get my hair done. All right.

name: LAURA
dialogue: That's how it is. All the way.

name: MARY
dialogue: I haven't heard much. I've been reading, I've been decorating, and I've been enchanting and making things. Tell me, what's the news with Thordak?

name: LAURA
dialogue: Well, he's terrible. He's even worse than we thought. Armies are marching on the city, and we plan on coming in from underneath, maybe striking at him where he doesn't realize. And we'd like your help, if you're willing.

name: MARY
dialogue: I don't think so. Oh, all right. Yes, I'd love to. I would love to. I've been craving dragon meat since Rimefang, so yes.

name: LAURA
dialogue: I don't know if we'll succeed, and I'm sure we won't all make it out alive. It's a big ask.

name: MARY
dialogue: (sighs) Isn't death supposed to be a wonderful adventure, as well?

name: LAURA
dialogue: I think so.

name: MARY
dialogue: Fuck it.

name: LAURA
dialogue: Fuck it.

name: MARY
dialogue: Fuck it. Durr 'n' durr. Fuck it. Let's do it. Yeah, all right. I've been sitting for too long; I need some action.

name: LAURA
dialogue: Did you make any dragon arrows?

name: MARISHA
dialogue: Buy her a drink first.

name: MARY
dialogue: I'll get back to you on it.

name: LAURA
dialogue: I plan on it. So many drinks.

name: MARY
dialogue: What next? What do we do?

name: LAURA
dialogue: We prepare tonight, and we leave tomorrow, I assume. You know us; we don't have a plan, really. I have no idea what's going on. Be prepared.

name: MARY
dialogue: Isn't that the secret to adulthood, that we're all winging it? Yes, all right. Good.

name: LAURA
dialogue: I'm glad you're joining.

name: MARY
dialogue: Darling, I'm with you wherever you go.

name: MATT
dialogue: With your recently joined into your crusade tiefling ally, you go to gather the rest of your party. Who's going to Kashaw? (laughter)

name: TALIESIN
dialogue: Kiki, what are you doing?

name: MATT
dialogue: You take a long, slow, careful walk down through town to the guard barracks.

name: MARISHA
dialogue: I try not to step on any cracks in the sidewalk on the way. It's very important.

name: MATT
